report.verdict: dead: first-player win rate outside 30-70% and Expert under 70% against Greedy, both as specified and after the one rule change
report.numbers: After the change (40 ends the match at the end of the round), whole-turn Expert: beats Random 99.5%, Greedy 58.4%, Racer 84.1% (400 games each, seats alternated, draws count half); first player wins 80.0% of 400 Expert mirror games; Expert equals Greedy in 57.5% of 9,720 decisions; 0 games hit the round cap; set positions pass. As specified (40 wins at once): Expert 97.8% / 54.0% / 74.3% against Random / Greedy / Racer, first player 92.0% of 400 Expert mirror games. Greedy mirror first player: 83.4% as specified, 71.8% after the change.
loop: Each turn a player sells one type of good (2.0 cards a sale at 4.3 a card in Expert play), Boosting it first when it can (0.34 a turn), and Crashes the good the other side is likely to sell (0.32 a turn); a match is a race to 40 in about four and a half turns each.

Reading the other hand matters: an Expert that saw his hand and knew he was Greedy beat Greedy 84% (100% as first player, 68% as second), against 58-67% for the honest Expert at 2,000 to 8,000 play-outs. So guessing what he holds is worth a lot, but the seat is worth more.

The first player wins 72-92% of mirrors with every bot and every Expert tried. Untested explanation: the first player sells each round first, and his Crash lands just before the second player sells, while the second player's Crash is half undone by the +1 at the round's end before the first player sells again.
report.cost: Coin rarely binds: it starts a turn at its cap of 6 in 11% of turns and ends at the cap in 3%, but 2.14 coin a turn goes unspent and an action card is priced out in only 9.9% of turns; the limit is the 5 action cards in a 20-card deck, not the coin.

ruleChange.to: reaching 40 ends the match at the end of that round; the higher score wins
ruleChange.why: In a four-turn race the first player's extra chance to cross 40 decided most games (92% in the Expert mirror); ending at the round's end gives both players the same number of sales. It brought the Expert mirror to 80-83%, still outside the line.
